objective_for_doctor:
Age: 18
Sex: Male
Chief Complaint: I have lower chest pain, bouts of choking or shortness of breath that wake you up at night, and swelling in one or more areas of your body

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Hi. I have lower chest pain, and I keep getting bouts of choking or shortness of breath that wake me up at night. I’m also having swelling in my legs—my left ankle and both calves/tibias are swollen—and I get short of breath when I exert myself.
[ASK] Do you have **fever with cough and/or shortness of breath**?
No, I don’t have fever. I do have shortness of breath, but it’s more like choking episodes that wake me up at night—I don’t specifically have a cough with fever.
[ASK] Do you have **chest pain or pressure that is brought on by exertion or stress and improves with rest**?
Yes. I get chest pain/pressure with exertion, and it feels worse when I’m active. It doesn’t really improve much with rest, but it is related to what I’m doing.
I’m not sure what you mean by “stable angina.” But I do have chest pain and I’ve been told I have angina before. It happens with activity.
I don’t know if it’s “unstable.” My chest pain and breathing problems have been happening in episodes, and I’m short of breath a lot, especially at night when I wake up choking.
I don’t know. I don’t have any specific information about pericarditis. I just have the lower chest pain and the breathing/choking episodes at night.
I’m not sure. I don’t have details about pericarditis—my main symptoms are lower chest pain and the night choking/shortness of breath with leg swelling.

No, I don’t think so—I haven’t been told I have pericarditis, and I don’t have any specific symptoms that I know are from that. My symptoms are mainly the lower chest pain and the choking/shortness of breath at night.
